questions.prompt: A bug in your agent wrote the wrong text into a recorded assistant message. With an event log, what is the right fix?
options: Find the bad fact and overwrite its text in place
Append a new fact that corrects or supersedes the bad one
Delete the bad fact and every fact recorded after it
Keep a second, corrected copy of the messages array beside the log
questions.explanation: An append-only log never changes or removes a recorded fact. Like a bank adding a correcting line, you add a new fact, so the history of the mistake stays visible.

questions.prompt: Why does keeping one list of facts avoid the problem of a messages array plus a separate debug log?
options: The list of facts takes less memory than an array
The model reads facts faster than messages
With only one record there is nothing for it to disagree with
Facts are frozen, so the model cannot change them
questions.explanation: Two records of the same conversation can drift apart when a bug updates one and not the other. When the log is the only record and everything else is computed from it, they cannot diverge.

questions.prompt: A later feature wants the model to see a shorter version of a long conversation. How does it do that without breaking the append-only rule?
options: It appends a new fact saying which shorter version to use from now on
It removes the oldest facts from the start of the list
It edits the oldest facts to contain shorter text
It starts a new empty log and copies only recent facts
questions.explanation: Old facts stay where they are. A new fact at the end says what to use from here on, so the full history is still there for anyone who needs it.
